goldens.comment: The ContextualLoggerMiddleware methods (QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) panic when a nil request is received. This occurs because they directly access req.PluginContext (via the instrumentContext function) without first checking if req is nil. This is a regression, as previous middleware layers gracefully handled nil requests.

The traceID is no longer logged for plugin requests. During a refactoring, the tracing import and the logic to extract and add traceID from the context to log parameters were removed from the LoggerMiddleware. The newly introduced ContextualLoggerMiddleware does not add this information, resulting in missing traceID in plugin request logs and impacting debugging and request tracing capabilities.

The `TestLogger.FromContext` method returns a new `TestLogger` instance via `NewTestLogger()` instead of returning the receiver (f). This causes logs to be recorded on an un-referenced instance, leading to broken test assertions that expect logs to be recorded on the original logger.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/plugins/log/ifaces.go:23 — Adding FromContext to the exported Logger interface breaks all external Logger implementations at compile time without a compatibility interface or migration path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger is being added to the Logger interface in pkg/plugins/log/ifaces.go. This is an exported interface (capital L), and adding a new method to an exported interface is a breaking change in Go - any external implementations of this interface will fail to compile. The diff shows implementations being added to TestLogger (fake.go) and grafanaInfraLogWrapper (logger.go), but external packages implementing Logger would break. This is a legitimate architectural/compatibility concern, though it may be intentional if this is an internal-only interface.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/metrics_middleware.go:149 — A missing or transient registry entry makes metrics instrumentation return before the plugin call, turning an observability failure into a request failure.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that a missing registry entry causes metrics instrumentation to return before the plugin call. Looking at the diff, the `instrumentPluginRequest` method at line 107 does return early with an error if `pluginTarget` fails (which happens when the plugin is not in the registry). However, this is NOT new behavior introduced by this diff - this is existing behavior that was already present in the original `instrumentation_middleware.go` file. The diff only renames the file and struct from `InstrumentationMiddleware` to `MetricsMiddleware` and removes the `instrumentContext` function (which was moved to the new `contextual_logger_middleware.go`). The error handling for missing registry entries is unchanged from the original code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/metrics_middleware.go:146 — The metrics middleware dereferences nil requests while the existing logger middleware explicitly forwards them, so malformed plugin calls now panic instead of reaching the client.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims the metrics middleware dereferences nil requests while the logger middleware forwards them. Looking at the diff, the metrics_middleware.go (renamed from instrumentation_middleware.go) does not show any new nil request handling issues - it processes requests the same way as before. The logger_middleware.go changes show it still has nil checks (lines 64-65, 77-78, 91-92, 105-106 show 'if !m.cfg.PluginLogBackendRequests' checks that return early). The metrics middleware code shown doesn't introduce any new nil dereference patterns - it accesses req.PluginContext and req.Queries which would have been accessed before the rename as well. This is not a new bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/contextual_logger_middleware.go:39 — The new context-enrichment path has no test proving endpoint, plugin, datasource, and user attributes reach the logger after the middleware split.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new ContextualLoggerMiddleware in contextual_logger_middleware.go that adds contextual attributes (endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, uname) to the context via instrumentContext(). This is new nontrivial logic that was previously part of the InstrumentationMiddleware. The diff shows no corresponding test file for contextual_logger_middleware.go being added, while the existing metrics_middleware_test.go only tests the metrics functionality. The finding correctly identifies that there's no test proving the context enrichment works correctly after the middleware split.
